references.text: Abraham gave his servant instructions not to take a wife for Isaac from the daughters of the Canaanites. Isaac now passes on the same instruction to Jacob.
Esau took wives from the daughters of Canaan, which was a source of grief to Isaac and Rebekah, underscoring the importance of Isaac's instructions to Jacob.
Rebekah expresses her displeasure at the thought of Jacob taking a wife from the daughters of Canaan, leading Isaac to send Jacob to Paddan-Aram.

Esau sees that Isaac has blessed Jacob and sent him to Paddan-Aram to find a wife, and that Jacob has obeyed his parents, which leads Esau also to try to gain favor by marrying within Abraham's family.
This verse shows the origin of Isaac's command; it is the same covenant requirement (not to marry Canaanites) that is passed from Abraham to Isaac and then to Jacob.
